Definition: from G4148; to be (or become) wealthy (literally or figuratively):--be increased with goods, (be made, wax) rich.
BiblicalUsage: Plouto means to be rich, to become wealthy. God fills the hungry with good things and sends the rich away empty in Luke 1:53, and Christ, though He was rich, for our sakes became poor, that we might be rich, in 2 Corinthians 8:9. Jesus tells Laodicea to buy gold tried in the fire, that she may be rich, in Revelation 3:18, and Romans 10:12 says the Lord is rich unto all that call upon Him.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe true riches run the other way — Christ became poor so I could be rich, and the rich sent away empty were full of themselves. My position is that I am rich only in Him.
